lem-ip-weighted-chi-square-triangular-ar:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice. For each $n$, let $G_{n,1},\ldots,G_{n,m_n}$ be independent standard normal random variables, and let $w_{n,j}\ge0$ satisfy $2\sum_{j=1}^{m_n}w_{n,j}^2=1$. If $\max_{1\le j\le m_n}w_{n,j}\to0$, then
$$T_n=\sum_{j=1}^{m_n}w_{n,j}(G_{n,j}^2-1)$$
has mean zero and variance one for every $n$ and converges in distribution to $N(0,1)$.
lem-ip-sparse-gaussian-extremal-profile:
## Statement

Let $0<q<2$, $\alpha,\beta>0$, $s=\alpha+\beta$, $L=qs-2\beta>0$, and $\kappa=L/(2-q)$. For $z>0$ define
$$a(z)=\frac{z^2\sinh(z^2)-q(\cosh(z^2)-1)}{(2-q)z^2},\qquad b(z)=\frac{z^2\sinh(z^2)-2(\cosh(z^2)-1)}{(2-q)z^q},\qquad \phi(z)=\frac{b(z)}{a(z)}.$$
Both $a$ and $b$ are positive, and for every $v\in\mathbb R$,
$$\cosh(zv)-1\ge a(z)v^2-b(z)|v|^q,$$
with equality at $v=0,z,-z$. The function $\phi:(0,\infty)\to(0,\infty)$ is continuous and strictly increasing onto its target. Put
$$z(x)=\phi^{-1}(x^L),\qquad \psi(z)=\frac1{2a(z)},\qquad d(x)=x^{2\beta}\psi(z(x))\quad(x>0).$$
For $C=[6(2-q)]^{1/(6-q)}$, its endpoint asymptotics are
$$z(x)\sim Cx^{L/(6-q)},\quad \psi(z)\sim z^{-2}\ (z\downarrow0),\quad d(x)\sim C^{-2}x^{2\beta-2L/(6-q)}\quad(x\downarrow0),$$
$$z(x)\sim x^\kappa,\quad \psi(z)\sim(2-q)e^{-z^2}\ (z\to\infty),\quad d(x)\sim(2-q)x^{2\beta}e^{-z(x)^2}\quad(x\to\infty).$$
There is a constant $C_1$ depending only on the parameters such that
$$\psi(z)z^2\le C_1,\quad \psi(z)(e^{z^2}-1)\le C_1\quad(z>0),\qquad \psi(z)^2(e^{z^2}-1)\le C_1e^{-z^2}\quad(z\ge1).$$
The following improper integrals are finite and positive:
$$c_0=\int_0^\infty d(x)^2(\cosh(z(x)^2)-1)\,dx,\quad c_1=\int_0^\infty d(x)z(x)^2x^{2\beta}\,dx,\quad c_2=\int_0^\infty d(x)z(x)^qx^{qs}\,dx,$$
$$M_1=\int_0^\infty x^{4\beta}d(x)z(x)^4\,dx,\qquad M_2=\int_0^\infty x^{2qs}d(x)z(x)^{2q}\,dx,$$
and $c_0=(c_1-c_2)/2$.

For positive real $n,h_0$, set $z_i=z(i/n)$ and $h_i=h_0d(i/n)$. Then $\sum_i h_i<\infty$, and for every finite real vector $(v_i)_{i\le m}$,
$$\sum_{i\le m}h_i(\cosh(z_iv_i)-1)\ge\frac{h_0}2\left(n^{-2\beta}\sum_{i\le m}i^{2\beta}v_i^2-n^{-qs}\sum_{i\le m}i^{qs}|v_i|^q\right).$$
As $n\to\infty$, the Riemann sums of the five displayed integral integrands, divided by $n$, converge to their respective integrals. In particular,
$$\sum_i h_i^2(\cosh(z_i^2)-1)\sim c_0h_0^2n,\quad \sum_i i^{2\beta}h_iz_i^2\sim c_1h_0n^{2\beta+1},\quad \sum_i i^{qs}h_iz_i^q\sim c_2h_0n^{qs+1},$$
$$\sum_i i^{4\beta}h_iz_i^4\sim M_1h_0n^{4\beta+1},\qquad \sum_i i^{2qs}h_iz_i^{2q}\sim M_2h_0n^{2qs+1}.$$

Let $\varepsilon>0$, $r>0$, and define the relaxed extremal value
$$J_\varepsilon(r)=\inf\left\{\sum_{i\ge1}g_i^2(\cosh(w_i^2)-1):\ 0\le g_i\le1,\ w_i\ge0,\ \sum_i i^{2\beta}g_iw_i^2\ge r^2\varepsilon^{-2},\ \sum_i i^{qs}g_iw_i^q\le\varepsilon^{-q}\right\}.$$
Choose $n,h_0>0$ by
$$c_1h_0n^{2\beta+1}=r^2\varepsilon^{-2},\qquad c_2h_0n^{qs+1}=\varepsilon^{-q},\qquad U^2=c_0h_0^2n.$$
Whenever $\varepsilon\downarrow0$, $r\to0$, $n\to\infty$, and $h_0\to0$, one has $J_\varepsilon(r)\sim U^2$. Writing
$$A=2\alpha+1/q-1/2,\qquad B=2s+1/q,\qquad D=\alpha+\beta(1-2/q)=L/q,$$
this gives
$$\sqrt{J_\varepsilon(r)}\sim c\varepsilon^{-A/D}r^{B/D},\qquad c=\frac{\sqrt{c_0}}{c_1}\left(\frac{c_1}{c_2}\right)^{-(2\beta+1/2)/L}>0.$$
The sufficient condition $n\to\infty$, $h_0\to0$ is equivalent to
$$r=o(\varepsilon^{a_c}),\qquad a_c=\frac{q\alpha+1-q/2}{q(\alpha+\beta)+1}.$$
The free coefficients $h_i$ need not be at most one. The upper bound on $J_\varepsilon$ is realized asymptotically by finitely supported feasible pairs, constructed by truncating the profile to compact coordinate windows and adjusting $n,h_0$. No probability statement or unrestricted all-radius power asymptotic is asserted.
lem-ip-finite-independent-array-fourth-m:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice, and suppose the probability law with density
$\phi(t)=(2\pi)^{-1/2}e^{-t^2/2}$ is supplied. Write
$\Phi(t)=\int_{-\infty}^t\phi(s)\,ds$; normalization is part of the given
probability-law hypothesis. For each positive integer $n$, let
$X_{n,1},\ldots,X_{n,k_n}$ be independent centered real random variables,
where $k_n$ is finite and each variable has a finite fourth moment. Different
rows need not share a probability space. Suppose

$$\sum_{j=1}^{k_n}\mathbb E X_{n,j}^2\longrightarrow v\in(0,\infty), \qquad \sum_{j=1}^{k_n}\mathbb E X_{n,j}^4\longrightarrow0.$$

Then, for $S_n=\sum_jX_{n,j}$,

$$\sup_{t\in\mathbb R}\left|\mathbb P(S_n\le t)-\Phi(t/\sqrt v)\right| \longrightarrow0.$$

The same conclusion applies to any specified sequence of finite arrays
satisfying these two limits; no identical-distribution hypothesis is needed.
def-ip-minimax-detection-risk-and-separa:
## Definition

Assume Countable Choice and use the Gaussian sequence inverse model with singular values $s_j>0$, inverse-noise weights $\sigma_j=s_j^{-1}$, and parameter coordinates $\theta=(\theta_j)\in\ell^2$. Let $a=(a_j)$ be a positive nondecreasing sequence with $a_j\to\infty$, and let $\sigma=(\sigma_j)$ be a positive nondecreasing sequence with $\sigma_j\to\infty$. For $\varepsilon>0$, put $\eta_j=\theta_j/\sigma_j$ and observe $Y_j=Z_j/\sigma_j=\eta_j+\varepsilon\xi_j$, where $Z$ is the normalized observation in the Gaussian sequence inverse model and the $\xi_j$ are independent standard normal random variables. For $0<q\le2$ and $r>0$, define
$$\Theta_q(r)=\left\{\eta\in\mathbb R^{\mathbb N}:(\sigma_j\eta_j)_{j\ge1}\in\ell^2,\ \sum_{j=1}^{\infty}|a_j\sigma_j\eta_j|^q\le1,\ \sum_{j=1}^{\infty}\sigma_j^2\eta_j^2\ge r^2\right\}.$$
Test $H_0:\eta=0$ against $H_1:\eta\in\Theta_q(r)$ by a product-Borel measurable randomized test $\psi:\mathbb R^{\mathbb N}\to[0,1]$, where $\psi(y)$ is the rejection probability. Its type-I error and maximal type-II error are
$$\alpha_\varepsilon(\psi)=\mathbb E_{\varepsilon,0}\psi,\qquad \beta_\varepsilon(\Theta_q(r),\psi)=\sup_{\eta\in\Theta_q(r)}\mathbb E_{\varepsilon,\eta}(1-\psi).$$
When $\Theta_q(r)=\varnothing$, define $\beta_\varepsilon(\Theta_q(r),\psi)=\beta_\varepsilon(\Theta_q(r),\alpha)=\gamma_\varepsilon(\Theta_q(r))=0$, the convention that no type-II error occurs when no alternative is possible. For $\alpha\in(0,1)$ define
$$\beta_\varepsilon(\Theta_q(r),\alpha)=\inf_{\psi:\,\alpha_\varepsilon(\psi)\le\alpha}\beta_\varepsilon(\Theta_q(r),\psi),\qquad \gamma_\varepsilon(\Theta_q(r))=\inf_\psi\{\alpha_\varepsilon(\psi)+\beta_\varepsilon(\Theta_q(r),\psi)\}.$$
A positive family $r_\varepsilon^*\to0$ is a minimax separation rate if $\gamma_\varepsilon(\Theta_q(r_\varepsilon))\to1$ and $\beta_\varepsilon(\Theta_q(r_\varepsilon),\alpha)\to1-\alpha$ for every $\alpha\in(0,1)$ whenever $r_\varepsilon/r_\varepsilon^*\to0$, while $\gamma_\varepsilon(\Theta_q(r_\varepsilon))\to0$ and $\beta_\varepsilon(\Theta_q(r_\varepsilon),\alpha)\to0$ for every $\alpha\in(0,1)$ whenever $r_\varepsilon/r_\varepsilon^*\to\infty$.
lem-ip-q2-ellipsoid-extremal-profile-exi:
## Statement

Assume the minimax detection-risk definition with $q=2$, and let $a_j$ and $\sigma_j$ be positive nondecreasing sequences tending to infinity. There is a constant $r_0>0$ such that for every $r\in(0,r_0)$ there exist $A,z_0>0$ with finite nonempty $S=\{j:Aa_j^2<1\}$ for which
$$\widetilde\eta_j^2=z_0^2\sigma_j^2(1-Aa_j^2)_+$$
satisfies
$$\sum_{j\ge1}\sigma_j^2\widetilde\eta_j^2=r^2,\qquad \sum_{j\ge1}a_j^2\sigma_j^2\widetilde\eta_j^2=1.$$
lem-ip-q2-ellipsoid-extremal-profile-is-:
## Statement

Assume the minimax detection-risk definition, $q=2$, and positive nondecreasing sequences $a_j$ and $\sigma_j$ with $a_j\to\infty$. Let $A,z_0>0$ and suppose $S=\{j:Aa_j^2<1\}$ is finite and nonempty. Define $\widetilde\eta_j^2=z_0^2\sigma_j^2(1-Aa_j^2)_+$ and assume
$$\sum_{j\ge1}\sigma_j^2\widetilde\eta_j^2=r^2,\qquad \sum_{j\ge1}a_j^2\sigma_j^2\widetilde\eta_j^2=1.$$
Then $\widetilde\eta\in\Theta_2(r)$ and minimizes $\sum_{j\ge1}\eta_j^4$ over $\Theta_2(r)$; the nonnegative minimizer is unique.
lem-ip-gaussian-product-mixture-testing-:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. In the Gaussian sequence detection experiment, let $v\in\Theta_q(r)$ have finite support $J$ and put
$$u(v)^2=\frac{1}{2\varepsilon^4}\sum_{j\in J}v_j^4.$$
Let $\pi_v$ be the uniform probability law on the finite family of mean sequences whose $j$th coordinate is independently $+v_j$ or $-v_j$ for $j\in J$ and is zero off $J$, and let $P_{\pi_v}$ be the corresponding mixture sampling law. Then its likelihood ratio with respect to the null law is
$$L_v=\frac{dP_{\pi_v}}{dP_{\varepsilon,0}}=\prod_{j\in J}\exp\!\left(-\frac{v_j^2}{2\varepsilon^2}\right)\cosh\!\left(\frac{v_jY_j}{\varepsilon^2}\right),$$
it satisfies
$$\mathbb E_{\varepsilon,0}L_v^2=\prod_{j\in J}\cosh\!\left(\frac{v_j^2}{\varepsilon^2}\right),\qquad \mathbb E_{\varepsilon,0}(L_v-1)^2\le \exp(u(v)^2)-1,$$
and the minimax risks obey
$$\gamma_\varepsilon(\Theta_q(r))\ge1-\frac12\sqrt{\exp(u(v)^2)-1},\qquad \beta_\varepsilon(\Theta_q(r),\alpha)\ge1-\alpha-\frac12\sqrt{\exp(u(v)^2)-1}$$
for every $\alpha\in(0,1)$.
thm-ip-sparse-detection-regime-split:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice and the minimax detection-risk definition with $0<q<2$, $a_j=j^\alpha$, $\sigma_j=j^\beta$, and $\alpha,\beta>0$. Let $r_\varepsilon\to0$ as $\varepsilon\downarrow0$, and put
$$\lambda=\frac{\alpha+\beta}{2}-\frac{\beta}{q}.$$
For $\lambda>0$, put $A=2\alpha+1/q-1/2$, $B=2(\alpha+\beta)+1/q$, and $D=\alpha+\beta(1-2/q)>0$. Choose any $\delta_\varepsilon>0$ with $\delta_\varepsilon\to0$ and $\delta_\varepsilon\log\varepsilon^{-1}\to\infty$, set $\widetilde r_\varepsilon=r_\varepsilon(1-\delta_\varepsilon)$, and define
$$u_\varepsilon^2=2\inf\left\{\sum_{j\ge1}h_j^2\sinh^2(z_j^2/2):\ 0\le h_j\le1,\ z_j\ge0,\ \sum_{j\ge1}j^{2\beta}h_jz_j^2\ge\frac{\widetilde r_\varepsilon^2}{\varepsilon^2},\ \sum_{j\ge1}j^{q(\alpha+\beta)}h_jz_j^q\le\frac1{\varepsilon^q}\right\}.$$
For each fixed significance level $\ell\in(0,1)$, the sharp errors have Gaussian form
$$\beta_\varepsilon(\Theta_q(r_\varepsilon),\ell)=\Phi(H_\ell-u_\varepsilon)+o(1),\qquad \gamma_\varepsilon(\Theta_q(r_\varepsilon))=2\Phi(-u_\varepsilon/2)+o(1),$$
where $\Phi(t)=(2\pi)^{-1/2}\int_{-\infty}^t e^{-x^2/2}\,dx$ and $H_\ell$ is its $(1-\ell)$-quantile. Moreover, if $r_\varepsilon=o(\varepsilon^{a_c})$ with $a_c=(q\alpha+1-q/2)/(q(\alpha+\beta)+1)$, then
$$u_\varepsilon\sim c_{\alpha,\beta,q}\,\varepsilon^{-A/D}r_\varepsilon^{B/D}$$
for a constant $c_{\alpha,\beta,q}>0$. Without this additional restriction on $r_\varepsilon$, the sharp error formulas above remain valid for every $r_\varepsilon\to0$, and a minimax separation rate is
$$r_\varepsilon^*=\varepsilon^{A/B}.$$
If $\lambda\le0$, for the same fixed significance level $\ell\in(0,1)$ put $n_\varepsilon=r_\varepsilon^{-1/\alpha}$ and $D_\varepsilon=n_\varepsilon^{-\beta}r_\varepsilon/\varepsilon-\sqrt{2\log n_\varepsilon}$. Then the sharp errors have degenerate form
$$\beta_\varepsilon(\Theta_q(r_\varepsilon),\ell)=(1-\ell)\Phi(-D_\varepsilon)+o(1),\qquad \gamma_\varepsilon(\Theta_q(r_\varepsilon))=\Phi(-D_\varepsilon)+o(1),$$
and a sharp separation-rate normalization is
$$r_\varepsilon^*=\Lambda\,\varepsilon^{\alpha/(\alpha+\beta)}(\log\varepsilon^{-1})^{\alpha/[2(\alpha+\beta)]},\qquad \Lambda=\left(\frac{2}{\alpha+\beta}\right)^{\alpha/[2(\alpha+\beta)]}.$$
Thus the sparse boundary $\lambda=0$ belongs to the degenerate regime, and the two regimes have different separation rates.

The deterministic globalized score-and-maximum family and the finite maximum tests constructed in the proof are asymptotically minimax in the Gaussian and degenerate regimes, respectively; the significance tests include deterministic randomization to satisfy the exact level constraint.
thm-ip-ellipsoid-detection-boundary:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice and the minimax detection-risk definition with $q=2$. For each $\varepsilon$, suppose $\Theta_2(r_\varepsilon)$ is nonempty and has a finite-support fourth-power minimizer $\widetilde\eta_\varepsilon$ with profile $\widetilde\eta_{\varepsilon,j}^2=z_0^2\sigma_j^2(1-Aa_j^2)_+$ as in the extremal-profile lemma. Put
$$u_\varepsilon^2=\frac{1}{2\varepsilon^4}\sum_j\widetilde\eta_{\varepsilon,j}^4,\qquad w_{\varepsilon,j}=\frac{\widetilde\eta_{\varepsilon,j}^2}{\sqrt{2\sum_j\widetilde\eta_{\varepsilon,j}^4}},\qquad w_{\varepsilon,0}=\max_jw_{\varepsilon,j},$$
and define
$$T_\varepsilon=\sum_jw_{\varepsilon,j}\bigl((Y_j/\varepsilon)^2-1\bigr),\qquad \psi_{\varepsilon,H}=\mathbf1_{\{T_\varepsilon>H\}}.$$
If $u_\varepsilon\to0$, then $\gamma_\varepsilon(\Theta_2(r_\varepsilon))\to1$ and $\beta_\varepsilon(\Theta_2(r_\varepsilon),\alpha)\to1-\alpha$ for every $\alpha\in(0,1)$. If $u_\varepsilon\to\infty$, then for every fixed $c\in(0,1)$ the tests $\psi_{\varepsilon,cu_\varepsilon}$ have total error tending to zero.

For the extremal profile, define the finite sums
$$J_1=\sum_j\sigma_j^4(1-Aa_j^2)_+,\quad J_2=A\sum_ja_j^2\sigma_j^4(1-Aa_j^2)_+,\quad J_0=\sum_j\sigma_j^4(1-Aa_j^2)_+^2.$$
The active constraints imply
$$r_\varepsilon^2=A\frac{J_1}{J_2},\qquad u_\varepsilon^2=\left(\frac{r_\varepsilon}{\varepsilon}\right)^4\frac{J_0}{2J_1^2}.$$
cor-ip-ellipsoid-sharp-gaussian-testing-:
## Statement

Assume the $q=2$ ellipsoid detection-boundary theorem, Countable Choice, and the Axiom of Choice. Along a sequence for which $u_\varepsilon$ is bounded above and bounded away from zero and $w_{\varepsilon,0}\to0$, the minimax level-$\alpha$ type-II error and minimax total error satisfy
$$\beta_\varepsilon(\Theta_2(r_\varepsilon),\alpha)=\Phi(H_\alpha-u_\varepsilon)+o(1),\qquad \gamma_\varepsilon(\Theta_2(r_\varepsilon))=2\Phi(-u_\varepsilon/2)+o(1),$$
where $\Phi$ is the standard normal distribution function and $H_\alpha$ is defined by $\Phi(H_\alpha)=1-\alpha$. Let $c_{\varepsilon,\alpha}=\inf\{t:\mathbb P_{\varepsilon,0}(T_\varepsilon\le t)\ge1-\alpha\}$; then $\mathbb P_{\varepsilon,0}(T_\varepsilon>c_{\varepsilon,\alpha})\le\alpha$ and $c_{\varepsilon,\alpha}\to H_\alpha$. The weighted tests with thresholds $c_{\varepsilon,\alpha}$ and $u_\varepsilon/2$ attain these asymptotics, while the uncalibrated threshold $H_\alpha$ has asymptotic size $\alpha$. The vanishing-largest-weight condition is required for this Gaussian sharp branch.
